content:
andrew: hitting intermittent gRPC stream stalls on inference-service -> embedder pods. Starts fine, then streams freeze for ~5-20s and then resume. Seen on node pairs across rack and same-node. Anyone else?

maya: yep noticed spikes on the p95 tail for streaming calls this morning. Correlates with high throughput on GPU nodes. logs show: `rpc error: code = Canceled desc = stream terminated` and lots of TCP retransmits.

josh: can you paste tcpdump? suspecting fragmentation / reassembly issue if MTU mismatch.

andrew: grabbed quick tcpdump between pods (host side):
```
20:12:03.123456 IP 10.2.3.4.58732 > 10.2.7.9.50051: Flags [P.], seq 321:1450, ack 421, win 257, options [TS val 123456 ecr 654321], length 1129
20:12:03.123457 IP (frag 1/2) 10.2.3.4 > 10.2.7.9: ip-proto-6 1500 bytes
20:12:03.123458 IP (frag 2/2) 10.2.3.4 > 10.2.7.9: ip-proto-6 350 bytes
```
Shows fragmented packets.

carla: but our CNI (calico) MTU is set to 1440, host NIC is 9000 on some racks -> mismatch. That can create mid-path fragmentation issues if GSO/TSO is on and offloading reassembly is inconsistent.

josh: also saw `ENOBUFS` on some nodes earlier (kernel ring buffer). Offload + kernel reassembly edge case. Try disable GSO on a test node: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off tso off gro off` and see if stream stall reproduces.

andrew: did that on node gpu-node-23, ran an A/B test with one pod pinned there. result: no stall after 30m under same load, p95 dropped ~30%.

maya: good. What about quick mitigation cluster-wide? Changing host NIC MTU to 1500 on all racks is risky. We could enable `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` to help PMTU discovery and roll a CNI MTU bump for problematic racks.

carla: short plan: 1) enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 on inference nodes (daemonset sysctl) 2) set calico MTU to 9000 on pods on racks where NIC is jumbo-capable OR normalize host NICs to 1500 (ops) 3) add a node-level check that compares `ip link` MTU vs CNI MTU and alert.

josh: also add a temporary k8s node annotation to disable GSO/TSO for canary nodes via a small privileged daemonset for quick rollback. That avoids rolling changes to physical NICs.

andrew: created a quick alert: `infra.mtu.mismatch` when abs(mtus) > 200. I'll deploy tcp_mtu_probing daemonset to two racks now as canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started: `mtu-probing-ds` -> 2/2 nodes updated.

sre-bot: detected 2 nodes with calico MTU != host MTU (gpu-node-21: host 9000 pod 1440, gpu-node-23: host 1500 pod 9000). Alert created #INC-2026.

maya: thanks — monitoring tail latencies. If probing helps we'll schedule a CNI config rollout and a remediation playbook.

andrew: notes for postmortem: root cause = inconsistent MTU + NIC offload causing fragmented TCP segments that sometimes fail reassembly in the kernel path leading to gRPC stream stalls. Mitigation = disable offloads or normalize MTU and enable MTU probing. Longer term: add preflight checks for CNI vs host MTU and include this in capacity onboarding for new racks.

carla: adding to runbook and ops checklist.

josh: can we also add iperf tests to the node health dashboard to catch fragmentation early?

andrew: yes adding `iperf3 -M 1440/9000` checks to health probe. will follow up with PR.

maya: great work team :thumbsup:
